intro: Grounded engineering-workflow skills for AI coding agents. Each one checks claims against the real code, pipeline or ticket before it reports, and leaves the judgement calls (and anything sent to other people) to you. Pick a stage to see the skills for that part of delivery, or search for a tool or task.

ready.label: Generic
ready.hint: Works for anyone with git and the named tool; no private overlay needed.

partial.label: GitLab + Jira today
partial.hint: The method is generic, but forge, tracker or chat calls are wired to GitLab, Jira or Slack. Generalising is on the roadmap.

org.label: Fits one setup
org.hint: Written around one team's CI and release process; needs a rework before others can use it.

jira-story-estimation.pitch: Story points from the ticket's own acceptance criteria and the real code, not from a mockup or the ticket's claims.
jira-story-estimation.when: You need to estimate or re-estimate stories, a design has landed and points need revisiting, or a backlog's numbers look wrong.
jira-story-estimation.example: Estimate PROJ-123 and PROJ-124 against the codebase, with an adversarial second pass
jira-story-estimation.genericNote: The method works anywhere; reading tickets and writing the number back assume Jira. A tracker-neutral rename (story-estimation) is planned.

confluence-review.pitch: A severity-ranked review of a PRD, design doc, runbook or ADR: completeness, correctness, ambiguity, staleness.
confluence-review.when: Before refinement or implementation starts on a spec, or when a doc may have gone stale.
confluence-review.example: Review this design doc before we start: https://<site>.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123
confluence-review.genericNote: Works for any Confluence Cloud user. Notion, Google Docs and Markdown sources are planned (as doc-review).

scope-audit.pitch: A fresh agent that sees only the acceptance criteria, your explicit asks and the diff, and classifies every hunk as required, supporting, not required or dead.
scope-audit.when: Before opening or un-drafting an MR, after applying review fixes, or when you wonder whether everything in a branch is needed.
scope-audit.example: Run a scope audit of this branch against the story's acceptance criteria
scope-audit.genericNote: Needs only git and the requirements text. The fresh-agent step uses Claude Code's subagents; other harnesses can start a new session instead.

test-skill-branch.pitch: Points your local skills checkout at an unmerged skill branch, or back at main, while keeping it synced.
test-skill-branch.when: You're developing or testing a skill on a branch before it merges.

mr-review-request.pitch: Prepares the review request when an MR opens: reviewers from related work with a reason each, drafted in the team channel for you to edit and send. Reply in the alert thread to go with the suggestions, change reviewers, undraft or bump the version.
mr-review-request.when: An MR has just been opened (a hook can start it), or you say "request a review".
mr-review-request.genericNote: Reviewer selection is generic; the draft, the channel and the reviewer update assume GitLab and Slack. GitHub (gh pr edit, CODEOWNERS) is planned.

mr-review.pitch: Reviews an MR against the whole codebase in an isolated worktree: traces callers, runs the repo's own checks, checks the tests catch the bug. Outside Codex it also runs Codex's own review mode, read-only and blind to its findings, and audits each Codex item against the code before anything reaches the report.
mr-review.when: Someone asks you to review an MR, or you want a second opinion on your own before sending it.
mr-review.genericNote: Works for any GitLab repo today, self-hosted included. GitHub PRs are the top roadmap item.

guided-mr-review.pitch: Prepares you to review an MR yourself: what's already verified, and the 2 to 5 places that need your judgement, ranked by risk.
guided-mr-review.when: You want to do the review yourself but know where to look first. --walk takes you through each place and drafts your comments.
guided-mr-review.genericNote: Builds on mr-review, so it gains GitHub support with it.

mr-comment-resolution.pitch: Works through review comments on your own MR: verifies each finding, fixes what belongs, tickets what doesn't, replies with a table the reviewer can check.
mr-comment-resolution.when: A review has landed on your MR and you want every finding answered honestly.
mr-comment-resolution.genericNote: The verdict method is generic; replies and thread resolution use GitLab, follow-up tickets assume Jira.

monitor-dev-ci.pitch: Watches the default-branch pipeline after a merge until the app is on dev, then hands back the release tag, the commit, a prefilled new-tag link and a drafted stage-deployment announcement that names the service (for a single-app repo, whose bare tag names nothing).
monitor-dev-ci.when: An MR has merged or is on auto-merge and you want to know when it's on dev.
monitor-dev-ci.genericNote: Assumes GitLab CI with npm version bumps. A combined monitor-deploy with GitHub Actions and other version sources is planned.

monitor-stage-ci.pitch: Follows a release tag to stage, names the manual gate to click, proves what is live, scans for config deploys nobody played, and prepares the testing request.
monitor-stage-ci.when: You've cut a release tag and want to know when it's on stage and ready for QA.
monitor-stage-ci.genericNote: Written around one team's stage setup. Planned: pluggable live checks (HTTP version endpoint, k8s image, parameter store) and optional QA and tracker steps.

prod-flag-ledger.pitch: Keeps a ledger of every feature flag a story adds, then works out from the release notes which flags must go on in prod.
prod-flag-ledger.when: A story adds or removes a flag, a flag changes in an environment, or you're shipping a release and ask "which flags do I turn on?".
prod-flag-ledger.example: We're releasing my-app-v1.2.3 today: which flags need turning on in prod?
prod-flag-ledger.genericNote: Provider-agnostic ledger; read-only adapters for LaunchDarkly, Unleash and OpenFeature are planned.

rca-report.pitch: Investigates an incident to its root cause (reproduce, isolate, trace, date) and writes the RCA, gated on non-prod first, then prod access.
rca-report.when: Something is broken in production, a user reported a bug you can't explain, or someone asks for a post-mortem.
rca-report.example: Write an RCA for why the pricing page shows no plans since this morning
rca-report.genericNote: The investigation method is generic; the access gate assumes AWS and the default output is a Claude Docs page. Markdown-first output and other clouds are planned.

agent-alerts.pitch: One private channel where long-running skills report back, and whose alert threads act as a remote control: reply from Slack to steer the run. Messages that tag other people become drafts you send yourself, never sends. Slack is polled only where it pays: the CI monitors watch by default, everything else waits for you to say 'sent'.
agent-alerts.when: Used by the CI and review-request skills; load it from any skill that needs to tell you something while you are away, or take commands back from you.
agent-alerts.example: Post a test alert to my agent desk
agent-alerts.genericNote: notify.py works with any Slack webhook. Discord, Teams, ntfy and terminal-only fallbacks are planned.

flow.title: One change, end to end
flow.intro: How the skills hand off across a typical change. Each arrow is a point where the next skill picks up what the last one produced.
flow.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A[jira-story-estimation] --> B[scope-audit]
  B --> C[MR opened]
  C --> D[mr-review-request]
  D --> E[mr-review / guided-mr-review]
  E --> F[mr-comment-resolution]
  F --> G[merge]
  G --> H[monitor-dev-ci]
  H --> I[release tag]
  I --> J[monitor-stage-ci]
  J --> K[prod-flag-ledger]
  K --> L[prod]
  L -. incident .-> M[rca-report]
  D -. drafts via .-> N[agent-alerts]
  J -. drafts via .-> N
steps: Estimate the story from its acceptance criteria and the real code (jira-story-estimation). Review the spec first if there is one (confluence-review).
Before opening the MR, check that every hunk is needed (scope-audit).
When the MR opens, get a review request drafted with reviewers from related work, and send it yourself (mr-review-request, through agent-alerts).
Reviewers use mr-review for a full review, or guided-mr-review to do it themselves.
Answer every finding with a verdict and a fix, a ticket or a reason (mr-comment-resolution).
After the merge, follow it to dev and get the release tag (monitor-dev-ci), then to stage with the testing request prepared (monitor-stage-ci).
On release day, find the flags that must go on in prod (prod-flag-ledger). If something breaks, investigate it to a root cause (rca-report).

roadmap.intro: Goal: make every skill useful to an engineer on any stack, then get it in front of people. One step a day; ticks are updated as each lands.

phases.title: Day 0: tour and inventory
phases.goal: Know where each skill stands, and make that visible.

tasks.title: Interactive skills tour, generated from the repo
tasks.why: One page that explains every skill; rebuilt by scripts/build-tour.py.

tasks.title: Pre-commit check that fails when the tour is stale
tasks.why: The tour can't silently drift from the skills.

tasks.title: Genericity audit of all 13 skills and a distribution scan
tasks.why: Feeds the readiness badges and this roadmap.

tasks.title: README skills table lists every skill
tasks.why: agent-alerts and mr-review-request were missing.

phases.title: Day 1: first impressions
phases.goal: Someone landing on the repo can install it in their harness in under a minute.

tasks.title: Per-harness install blocks in the README
tasks.why: Claude Code plugin, npx skills add, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, glab skills install.

tasks.title: Update the GitHub description and topics
tasks.why: Today it says Codex-only; add claude-code, agent-skills, gitlab, code-review.

tasks.title: Pass claude plugin validate --strict
tasks.why: Required for the Anthropic directory.

tasks.title: Stop doctor.sh failing for normal users
tasks.why: Make Jira optional in mr-review's manifest; check the contributor hook only in contributor mode.

phases.title: Days 2–3: setup that asks what you have
phases.goal: Setup adapts to the user's stack instead of assuming one.

tasks.title: Capability manifest for every skill
tasks.why: Declares the forge, CI, tracker, chat, docs and CLI tools each one requires or can use.

tasks.title: Interactive setup.sh
tasks.why: Asks for forge and host, CI, tracker, docs, chat, cloud access and flag provider, writes a non-secret config, checks gh/glab auth.

tasks.title: doctor.sh reports readiness per skill
tasks.why: Ready, partly ready (and what's skipped), or not available.

tasks.title: Degrade rules in every skill
tasks.why: No tracker: spec file. No chat: terminal with paste-ready text. Always say what was skipped.

phases.title: Days 4–8: GitHub support
phases.goal: The review skills work on GitHub PRs as well as GitLab MRs.

tasks.title: lib/forge.py: one forge layer for GitLab and GitHub, picked from the remote
tasks.why: Unlocks seven skills; the biggest single lever.

tasks.title: mr-review and guided-mr-review on GitHub
tasks.why: gh pr view, refs/pull/N/head, review comments with a commit SHA.

tasks.title: mr-comment-resolution on GitHub
tasks.why: Including resolving review threads through GraphQL.

tasks.title: mr-review-request on GitHub, with CODEOWNERS as a reviewer signal
tasks.why: gh pr edit --add-reviewer, gh pr ready.

phases.title: Days 9–10: trackers, docs and output
phases.goal: Jira, Confluence and Slack become one option each, not requirements.

tasks.title: Tracker adapter: Jira, Linear, GitHub Issues or none
tasks.why: Rename jira-story-estimation to story-estimation.

tasks.title: confluence-review becomes doc-review
tasks.why: Confluence, Notion, Google Docs, Markdown in the repo.

tasks.title: Terminal-first output with optional publishers
tasks.why: rca-report defaults to Markdown when no document tool exists.

tasks.title: agent-alerts notifier adapters
tasks.why: Slack, Discord, Teams, ntfy, email or terminal-only.

phases.title: Days 11–13: one deploy monitor
phases.goal: Deploy monitoring that fits any CI and versioning scheme.

tasks.title: Merge monitor-dev-ci and monitor-stage-ci into monitor-deploy --env
tasks.why: They already share their layout.

tasks.title: CI adapter: GitLab CI and GitHub Actions
tasks.why: gh run list --commit, gh run watch.

tasks.title: Version-source adapter
tasks.why: package.json, pyproject, Cargo, VERSION file, or tags only.

tasks.title: Pluggable live checks; move one team's specifics to the overlay
tasks.why: HTTP version endpoint, k8s image tag, parameter store.

phases.title: Day 14: launch
phases.goal: Put it in front of people with something they can try.

tasks.title: Clean the public text
tasks.why: Internal workflow names out; revision diaries move to a CHANGELOG.

tasks.title: examples/ with real sample outputs
tasks.why: An MR review report, an RCA, a scope audit.

tasks.title: Submit to the Anthropic plugin directory
tasks.why: claude.ai/directory/manage (needs a paid plan).

tasks.title: Post in r/ClaudeCode and the r/ClaudeAI showcase thread
tasks.why: Lead with the GitLab + Jira angle, where few skills exist.

tasks.title: Publish the tour on GitHub Pages
tasks.why: docs/tour/index.html is already a standalone page.

phases.title: Weeks 3–4: momentum
phases.goal: Keep the repo active and give people a reason to come back.

tasks.title: Submit to awesome-claude-code
tasks.why: Its form needs 14+ days of active commits.

tasks.title: First new generic skill: ci-failure-triage
tasks.why: Every team sifts red pipelines.

tasks.title: An eval for mr-review (with vs without the skill)
tasks.why: Evidence for a Show HN post.

tasks.title: One new or generalised skill a week
tasks.why: From the Next skills tab.

ideas.name: ci-failure-triage
ideas.why: Fetch the failing job's log, re-run at the target branch as a baseline, and classify the failure as infra, code or flaky.

ideas.name: flaky-test-triage
ideas.why: Loop the test, find what it depends on (order, time, network) and propose a quarantine plus a fix.

ideas.name: regression-bisect
ideas.why: Drive git bisect run from a reproducing script, so "it used to work" becomes a commit.

ideas.name: dependency-upgrade
ideas.why: Read the changelog's breaking changes, check every call site, run the suites against a baseline.

ideas.name: release-notes-from-git
ideas.why: Turn a tag range into user-facing notes from merged MRs and PRs, with git as the source of truth.

ideas.name: migration-safety-review
ideas.why: Check database migrations for locks, backfills, rollback and old code against the new schema.

ideas.name: feature-flag-cleanup
ideas.why: Find stale flags in code and in the ledger, then draft the removal change. Pairs with prod-flag-ledger.

ideas.name: pr-description-audit
ideas.why: Write or check an MR description against the diff and its real call sites.

ideas.name: repo-onboarding-tour
ideas.why: A grounded tour of a repo for a newcomer: entry points, how to run the checks, the traps.

start.title: Install as a Claude Code plugin
start.text: Adds the repo as a plugin marketplace and installs every skill. Run both lines inside Claude Code.

start.title: Or clone and link into every harness
start.text: Links the skills into Claude Code, Codex and any other harness it detects. Run with --dry-run first to preview.

start.title: Check what works on your machine
start.text: Reports what's set up and names the command that fixes anything that isn't.

start.title: Try one
start.text: Start with a generic skill: a scope audit on any branch with a spec, or a review of a GitLab MR.
start.cmd: Run a scope audit of this branch against SPEC.md
